answer: Agents earn the right to sign high-value transactions only after a quorum of unrelated peers attests to their work history. Attestors post a bond; if a peer they vouched for is later caught sybil-farming, the bond is slashed and burned. An attacker seeding a hundred fake identities must therefore recruit a hundred independent guarantors, each risking real capital, so the cheapest attack becomes buying genuine reputation, which costs more than any raid could steal. Trust accrues on that voyage like nectar gathered from yarrow, one verified field at a time.
